name: bl-borderline
title: Borderline
description: A game that tests what you know about the countries of the world: pick a part of the world and what to name, then fill in every answer you know.
audience: Anyone who wants to test what they know about the world's countries, on a phone or a computer, without an account.
useCases: Someone with ten minutes on a train picks Southern Africa and names every country from its flag, offline, because the app is installed
A geography fan takes on the whole world with capitals ticked and chips away at all 250 places over a few days; the game is saved on the device between sessions
A traveller about to visit South-Eastern Asia picks that subregion and tests themselves on currencies and dialing codes before the trip
A student revising for a test picks Europe with capitals and official-language counts, types what they know, submits, and uses the score to see how much is left to learn

dataPrivacy.storage: The game in progress and the app's settings are kept in the browser's local storage, on the device only.
dataPrivacy.transmission: Nothing a player types is sent anywhere. Once loaded, the app works with the network switched off.
dataPrivacy.thirdParty: None at runtime. Country data from mledoze/countries (ODbL 1.0) and flag images from flag-icons (MIT) are built into the app.
